Date: 2025-09-09

Attendees: Ben Carter (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Samir Khan (Atlas Head of ML), Lina Martinez (Eng Manager), Jacob Reed (Security), Priya Nair (Product)

transcript:
00:00 Ben (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We are starting the weekly POC sync, I see Samir, Lina, Jacob, Priya — thanks for making time. Maya and I are from Redwood. Quick agenda: regression results, prompt set changes, guardrails, and then next steps.
00:22 Samir (Head of ML): Yeah thanks Ben, really excited to go through the quality numbers. We ran the scoring over the 450 prompt set yesterday, there are a few regressions we flagged.
00:35 Maya (SE): Cool, can you call out the top regressions? I pulled your earlier sheet, I saw a bump on the summarization prompts.
00:42 Samir: Right, so on the summarization bucket — about 12% drop in ROUGE-L compared to last week when you switched the default model variant, so worth looking at prompt phrasing and length. Some of that might be truncation.
00:56 Lina (Eng Manager): Do you have timestamps or sample outputs we can look at? The product team saw more omissions.
01:04 Priya (Product): I pulled three examples and added them to the sheet under examples tab, but I also noticed more factual hallucinations in the recipe/customer support prompts, like invented phone numbers.
01:18 Jacob (Security): Quick sec question — are those examples coming from production traffic or synthetic tests? We need to understand data residency for those test logs.
01:27 Samir: Mostly synthetic + anonymized production; we removed PII but left structure.
01:33 Ben: Ok, for the regressions Maya, could you recap what changed last week on the Redwood side? We swapped quantization profile and bumped beam/penalty defaults right?
01:43 Maya: Yeah so we trialed the q4_1-ish quantization profile and enabled a more aggressive prompt batching optimization to hit cost targets. The tradeoff can be more tokenization edge cases — results can vary for long context. Also we set the default sampling temp lower, which tightened outputs but may increase omission.
02:05 Samir: That rings true. The fails are mostly long-context summarizations and multi-step instructions. Short Q&A seems fine.
02:15 Ben: Good data point. For immediate mitigations, we can try two things: add length-preserving prompt templates and enable prefix caching for those long context routes, and run the regression on the dedicated profile where we can increase kv cache and reduce batch size.
02:31 Lina: Dedicated vs hosted — what's the expected latency delta if we move to dedicated for the regression? We need numbers to present to the CTO.
02:39 Maya: On our internal numbers, dedicated with reserved GPUs typically reduces p95 by ~30% for long-context workloads vs the cost-optimized hosted runtime we used for the weekly run. But cost goes up. We can run a 24-hour benchmark and produce p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost/token deltas.
02:55 Samir: That would be helpful. Also is it possible to keep the hosted config but tweak quantization to be less aggressive?
03:02 Maya: Yes we can back off quantization to q4_0 or enable mixed precision for specific model layers — that'll increase token cost by a bit but should reduce omission.
03:12 Priya: On the guardrails side — we need stronger hallucination checks. Can Redwood run a post-process filter to detect improbable facts (like phone numbers or invented addresses) and flag them?
03:22 Maya: We have a two-layer approach: RL/heuristic filters plus a lightweight fact-checker that runs a verification model against a small knowledge source. For POC we usually add a conservative filter that strips numeric-looking strings unless they match patterns we expect. It's configurable.
03:38 Jacob: Will that introduce latency? We need to keep the p95 under 1.2s for our chat use-case or it breaks UX.
03:45 Maya: The lightweight pattern filters are sub-10ms. The verification model adds ~80-120ms depending on the host; if that pushes p95 above your threshold we can run verification asynchronously and show a validation badge, or we can run it only for high-risk intents.
03:58 Lina: Async verification sounds promising but the UX team needs clear signal if content is pending verification.
04:06 Ben: We'll add UX notes to the action items. Back to scoring — Samir, you mentioned the scoring rubric looked noisy. Can you outline the main scoring buckets again?
04:16 Samir: Sure: relevance (0-5), factuality (0-5), completeness (0-5), style/brand (0-3). We combine into a weighted score. The regressions were mostly in factuality and completeness.
04:28 Priya: Are the annotators consistent? Inter-annotator variance sometimes explains 5-ish percent swings.
04:35 Samir: We re-calculated Krippendorff alpha this week — it was 0.71 overall, lower on the summary bucket (0.62). So some variance but still meaningful.
04:46 Maya: For the short term we can add automated heuristics to reduce noisy examples from the eval set and run a filtered regression, then run manual checks on a smaller stratified sample.
04:55 Ben: Good. Also, we found a few transcription errors in the earlier export — just flagging that sometimes Fireflies misc transcriptions swap product names; we saw 'Reddock' instead of 'Redwood'.
05:05 Samir: Ha, yes saw that. Noted.
05:09 Lina: Let's talk about prompt edits. Priya, you volunteered to gather more edge cases — what's the plan?
05:16 Priya: I'll add 50 edge-case prompts to the sheet, focusing on long, multi-step and embedded lists. I'll mark high-risk intents.
05:24 Ben: Perfect. Maya, on the regression run — can you run two experiments: one on hosted with less aggressive quant, another on dedicated with current quant, and compare? Also include the prefix cache on for long-context route.
05:38 Maya: Yep, I'll run host-quant-backoff and dedicated-current. I'll include p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, and a confusion matrix for the top failure types. Expect results by next Tuesday 2025-09-16.
05:50 Jacob: Security asks: we're tracking SOC 2 in-scope for this pilot, and we may need KMS integration so logs don't include plaintext prompts. Can Redwood support envelope encryption pointing to our KMS?
06:03 Maya: Yes, we support BYOK via customer-managed KMS for the Private and Dedicated deployments; hosted can also be configured with a customer key for at-rest encryption, but we need to verify if HSM-backed KMS is required. We'll get an engineer to confirm the exact flow.
06:17 Jacob: Also SSO — SAML is required for our internal users.
06:21 Ben: We have SAML/SCIM support in our console; we'll share the SSO setup guide.
06:27 Jacob: And audit log retention — can we push logs to your SIEM or do you support pushing to our S3?
06:33 Maya: We support log delivery to customer S3 and can integrate with partners (Datadog/CloudWatch) for metric forwarding. Full audit logs for Dedicated/Private a bit more straightforward.
06:44 Samir: One more note: our ops team suggested testing a smaller beam size too. Could that help with omissions?
06:50 Maya: Beam tends to help diversity but for hallucinations it can sometimes hurt; lowering beam and increasing temperature can increase creativity but also hallucination. It's a balance — we'll include beam sweep in the experiment matrix.
07:02 Ben: Great. Let's cover the regression scoring artifacts — I'll consolidate the prompt_set_v3.csv and the scoring rubric and share today. Samir, can you re-run the automated scoring with the filtered set once Ben pushes the updated prompt set?
07:16 Samir: Yep we'll re-run overnight.
07:20 Priya: UI signal for verification — I'll mock up a simple badge and state transitions and share in Figma.
07:27 Lina: Regarding benchmarks, if dedicated tests look good we'll need an internal business case. Ben, can you provide cost estimates per 100k tokens for both modes?
07:35 Ben: Yes I'll include cost/token deltas and an estimated monthly spend for your expected query volume.
07:40 Samir: Any competitor behavior we should be aware of? We've run a quick OpenAI baseline — lower hallucination in short Q&A but higher cost at our scale. Anthropic did well on style constraints but worse on multi-step completion.
07:56 Maya: Noted. We'll include competitor baselines in the benchmark doc.
08:05 Ben: Ok last section, timeline and next steps recap.
08:11 Ben: Action items recap: Ben share prompt set + cost estimates (due 2025-09-11), Maya run two regression experiments + results (due 2025-09-16), Jacob confirm security list and KMS requirement (due 2025-09-12), Priya gather 50 edge prompts and mock UX badge (due 2025-09-15), Samir re-run scoring on updated set (target 2025-09-12).
08:36 Samir: Sounds good. Any blockers?
08:39 Jacob: None from security yet beyond confirming KMS and retention windows.
08:44 Maya: We might ask to spin up a short dedicated slot for the benchmark; will reach out to your infra contact after this call.
08:53 Ben: We'll send calendar invite for the benchmark slot and share the docs. Thanks everyone.
08:58 Priya: Thanks all.
09:00 Ben: End of recording.
